source.title: The Memory Perturbation Equation: Understanding Model's Sensitivity to Data
source.authors: Peter Nickl; Lu Xu; D. Tailor; Thomas Möllenhoff; Mohammad Emtiyaz Khan

record.file_problem: The full paper text, including appendices, is present; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether data-sensitivity estimates track held-out generalization, using leave-one-out and leave-one-class-out estimates compared with test performance. It does not test the specific interventions or measurements named in V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The paper reports sensitivity-based estimates of test NLL and compares them with held-out test NLL, including during training. This bears on the broad claim about properties tracking generalization, but none of the mapped versions names the sensitivity measures used here. Cited findings from prior work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Although the main experiments evaluate sensitivity estimates, auxiliary results compare convolutional and fully connected networks on the same image datasets and bear on V3. The sensitivity-estimation results themselves test none of V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors present MPE as a framework unifying and extending sensitivity measures, demonstrate prediction of held-out performance including during training, and emphasize matching sensitivity measures to the training algorithm. Comparisons with other generalization measures remain future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes and evaluates a Bayesian-derived sensitivity framework and compares its estimates with retraining and held-out performance; it does not reproduce the listed versions' interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The quality of generalization estimates varies with the sensitivity approximation and optimizer: iBLR estimates track test NLL better than the tested SGD-based diagonal-GGN and K-FAC estimates; the Adam estimate is reported to improve with smaller batch size.

fits_no_version.finding: MPE-derived LOO estimates closely track test NLL across regularization settings; tracking during training depends on the optimizer and sensitivity approximation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Algorithm-suited sensitivity estimates can predict held-out NLL across regularization settings and training stages in the tested models.

fits_no_version.finding: Estimated leave-one-class-out loss correlates with test NLL after class removal and retraining on Fashion-MNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MPE-derived LOCO estimates predict variation in test NLL following whole-class removal in the tested models.

record.problems: Several comparisons are reported qualitatively from figures without numerical correlation statistics or uncertainty intervals. The sensitivity estimates depend on approximations; the authors report poor results for diagonal-GGN and weaker results for K-FAC than iBLR, and note that some estimates deteriorate with overfitting.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows left out. Hyperparameter values selected to obtain a good prediction, such as the iBLR h0 grid search, are setup choices rather than separate reported outcomes.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance under random versus natural labels.
Width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
The contribution of local connectivity, learning sparse local connections, initialization from a trained convolutional network, and comparisons on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and SVHN.
A matched adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison under the specified tuning budgets, including recovery interventions.
A large-batch penalty beyond a workload-dependent threshold under fixed epoch budgets and its recovery. Figure 10 primarily evaluates estimator fidelity at batch sizes 8 and 32.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on dataset size, configuration and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing examples selected by label memorization versus removing equally many random examples.

missing.what: Architecture comparison with momentum SGD: MNIST MLP (500, 300) has 99.9% training and 98.4% test accuracy; LeNet5 has 99.2% training and 99.1% test accuracy. Fashion-MNIST MLP (32, 16) has 89.9% training and 86.2% test accuracy; LeNet5 has 95.0% training and 91.2% test accuracy. Record these separately from LOCO-estimator correlations.
missing.locator: Appendix I.3, Table 3; Appendix I.2 for training procedure

missing.what: MNIST architecture comparison during generalization-estimation experiments: iBLR test accuracies are 95.6% for MLP (32, 16) and 97.5% for LeNet5; SGD runs report 95.8% and 97.4%, respectively. Diagonal-GGN and K-FAC entries are estimator configurations, not distinct optimizer families.

MNIST Adam architecture comparison: at batch size 8, MLP (32, 16) reaches 97.3% test accuracy and LeNet5 99.2%; at batch size 32, the corresponding accuracies are 97.4% and 99.2%. Record the differing regularization settings.

record.verdict_notes: The reader correctly left R1–R7 unlinked but overlooked auxiliary architecture comparisons bearing on V3. All supplied rows receive cannot_determine relative to the claim versions; this does not dispute their reported estimator-performance findings.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or held-out chance-accuracy comparison.
No width sweep past the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD held-out-performance comparison.
No large-batch versus small-batch generalization comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
No removal of examples selected for memorization compared with random-example removal.

relationships.condition: MNIST, LeNet5 versus fully connected MLPs
relationships.reason: Unrecorded results in Appendix I.3 show test accuracy of 99.1% for LeNet5 versus 98.4% for MLP (500, 300) with momentum SGD; Tables 5 and 7 also favor LeNet5 over MLP (32, 16). This verdict rests on the text, not R1–R7.
relationships.display_finding: The reported higher LeNet5 test accuracy remains unverified across different architecture-specific training schedules.
